title: I vibe coded a roguelike zombie game, someone made a YouTube video playing it, and I started getting players
author: khaterdev
selftext:
I vibe coded a mobile game without using any known game engine. It runs on a custom C++ game engine built by Claude that works cross platform with excellent performance. Claude helped me do a lot of research, and that research was followed for everything. The game was completely built and tested by Opus 5.5 in 10 days. It also created the videos, screenshots and store listings, and pushed it for review.

It took a few days to get approved on Google Play. On the App Store it waited for review for 2 weeks, then when it was finally In Review, it took 8 minutes to get approved on the first try. Well, Opus knew how to get it approved by filling in all the forms, videos, images and everything correctly for me.

Of course, I had no players other than me, a few friends and a few people who found it on the store, until today I woke up to 65+ new players and 9 of them online playing. I thought maybe the store pushed it through ASO, but the players were on both Android and iOS. So I searched Google and found that someone with 20k+ followers on YouTube made a video playing the game for 10 minutes.

That was my only lead, and his 300+ views converted into 60+ players for me.

No money yet of course, other than $0.03 on AdMob. I don't push any purchases hard on new players and I don't force any ads. Both ads and purchases are only offered after some time in the game, as the research suggested. So it is too early to assume anything, even for those 60+ players, because most of them saw nothing to buy and most of them were not offered any ads yet.

But since little Opus also built me a game server for analytics (with a lot of anonymous and data deletion options for players in Europe and some other countries, if they choose to), I got some nice intelligence into the gameplay from real players:

\- About half of the new players played 10+ minutes, 1 in 4 played 30+ minutes, and 8 played more than an hour on their first day. One player in Thailand played for 3.6 hours (18 runs, 8 wins).

\- The controls are not the problem. The median player moves within 1.8 seconds and picks up their first gem in 8 seconds.

\- After a run ends, the most pressed button is Upgrades, then Play Again. Only a few went back to the menu.

\- Players picked 591 spell fusions, and they decided in under a second most of the time, so they clearly know what they want.

\- The problem is the first run. The median first run lasts 3.3 minutes, only 16% reach the first boss at 5:00, and only 2% win it. Players get hit about 2 times a minute, mostly by runners and spitters.

\- About 1 in 4 players played just one run and stopped.

So what we are doing about it: the game's bot used for balancing was way too good. It won 25% of first runs while real players win 2%. So Opus built a human-like bot (slower reactions, panics, misses spit, picks random cards sometimes) and fitted a bot twin to every real player's first 3 runs from the server data. Now we are using those twins to test a real-time difficulty system for the first 3 runs only. It watches how you are doing, and if you keep getting hit, it quietly eases things: fewer zombies, slower runners and spit, a longer recovery after a hit, more heart drops and a wider gem pull. If you are not getting hit, it does nothing, so players who already play well get the normal game. It turns off for good after your first win, and it never touches the Weekly or the leaderboards.

The target from the research is 70-80% of new players reaching the first boss and 25-40% winning the first chapter. When the bots hit those numbers, it goes live to half of the new players first, and the server will tell us if it actually keeps more people playing.

What do you think I should do next? Should I run ads? What platform?

You can also find the game here if you ever want to check the game play or the store listings Opus built for me:
